Here are three short samples of my writing. Match my style in what you write.

making them play lame chicken.... Now all this done by a young lady who remembers eighteen months ago with so much regret that she has lost so much of her high spirits--might argue that her spirits were before tremendous; and yet they were not. That other Sarah was ladylike, I am sure, in her wildest moments, but there is something hurried and boisterous in this one's tricks that reminds me of some one who is making a merit of being jolly under depressing circumstances. No! that is not a nice Sarah now, to my taste.

The commencement of '61 promised much pleasure for the rest of the year, and though Secession was talked about, I do not believe any one anticipated the war that has been desolating our country ever since, with no prospect of terminating for some time to come. final_message:
We had company on Tuesday, and I am still not over it. Three of them, all at once, and without a word of warning; just the sound of wheels on the gravel and then the dog going wild, and I knew before I reached the window that my quiet week was at an end.

It was Margaret, her sister Anne, and a cousin I had not laid eyes on since the spring of the year before last, who has grown stout and loud and, I must confess, a good deal more agreeable than I remembered. I stood in the doorway in my oldest apron, with flour to the elbow, and was kissed on both cheeks before I could so much as apologize for my appearance. Apologies were waved away. "We have come to see you, not your dress," said Margaret. Very kind, I am sure; but I noticed she looked at the dress all the same.

Now, there was nothing in the house fit to set before three hungry travelers. I had a heel of bread, a little cold mutton, and some pickled beets that I would not have offered a stranger. And yet we sat down to it as though it were a feast! Anne declared the beets the best she had ever tasted, which I take to be the polite untruth of a well-brought-up woman, and the cousin ate hers and half of mine. That is friendship, I suppose: to be thought well of on the strength of a poor supper.

We talked until the lamp burned low. Of who had married, and who had not, and who ought to have thought twice; of the price of everything; of the old house on the hill and whether it would ever be lived in again. Margaret cried a little over her brother, and then laughed at herself for crying, and then we all did both together, which is a thing I never could explain to a man.

How quiet it is now! They left this morning, and the dog has taken to lying in the doorway with his nose toward the road, as if he thought they might return. I do not blame him. I caught myself setting out four cups at breakfast, and had to put the extra one back very quietly, so that no one should see.

Did I want my quiet week? I thought so. I am less certain now. Come again, all of you, and bring nothing but yourselves; I will see to the beets.
